name: Zostel Leh
summary: Zostel's Leh hostel offers dorm beds and private rooms within walking distance of Main Bazaar, with a common area where solo travellers find shared taxi partners for Nubra and Pangong. It suits students and backpackers resting their first two days at 3,500 m.
body: Zostel is one of India's best-known hostel chains, and its Leh property follows the usual pattern: mixed and female dorms, a few private rooms, a cafe or common kitchen area, and staff who can point you to bike rentals, permit agents and shared jeeps. Being close to the town centre matters in Leh, because for the first 48 hours you should not be walking far or climbing much.

Expect hostel standards: shared bathrooms in dorms, hot water that may depend on solar heating or set hours, and power cuts that are normal in Ladakh. The common area is the main reason to stay. In June and July many travellers post on the board looking for people to share a car to Pangong or Tso Moriri, which can cut your costs by half.
why: Cheapest reliable bed near Main Bazaar
Easy to find travel partners for shared cars
Staff used to first-time Ladakh travellers
price_band: ₹700–1,500 for a dorm bed; ₹2,500–4,500 a night for a private double (indicative)

faqs.q: Does Zostel Leh have private rooms?
faqs.a: Yes, alongside dorm beds it has a small number of private rooms, some with attached bathrooms. They fill early in June, July and August, so book ahead online. Prices change with season and demand.

faqs.q: Is Zostel Leh good for acclimatisation days?
faqs.a: Yes. It is close enough to Main Bazaar that you can eat and shop without long walks or taxis, and the common area is a comfortable place to rest. Ask for a lower-floor bed or room for your first night if you can.

faqs.q: Is Zostel Leh safe for solo women?
faqs.a: Zostel generally offers female-only dorms in its larger hostels, and Leh is considered one of the safer destinations in India for solo women. Check the current room types when booking, keep valuables in a locker, and use registered union taxis at night.

name: Turtuk Balti homestays
summary: Turtuk is a homestay village: dozens of Balti families in Youl and Farol, the two halves of the village, rent simple rooms with dinner and breakfast. It is the best way to taste Balti food and village life on the Shyok.
body: Turtuk opened to tourists only in 2010, and most accommodation is still in family houses. Rooms are plain, often on the upper floor around a courtyard or apricot garden, with carpets, thick quilts and a shared or simple attached bathroom. Hot water usually comes in a bucket. Dinner is eaten with the family or brought to your room: rice, dal, vegetables, sometimes Balti dishes made with buckwheat or apricot.

We do not name single homestays because standards and ownership change. Instead, walk across the footbridge into the village, look at two or three rooms, and agree the price including meals before you put your bags down. Expect conservative norms: modest clothing, no alcohol, and photography of women only with permission.
why: Meals cooked by Balti families
Walk straight out into orchards and lanes
Money goes directly to village households
price_band: ₹1,200–2,000 per person a night with dinner and breakfast (indicative)

faqs.q: How do I book a homestay in Turtuk?
faqs.a: Most Turtuk homestays do not need booking outside July and August. Arrive by early afternoon, walk into the village and look at a few rooms. Your Leh guesthouse or driver can also phone ahead. Agree the price and meals before you check in.

faqs.q: Do Turtuk homestays have attached bathrooms?
faqs.a: Some do, many do not. Expect simple bathrooms, sometimes shared, with hot water in buckets on request. A few newer guesthouses at the village edge have attached bathrooms and showers at a slightly higher price.

faqs.q: Is food included in Turtuk homestays?
faqs.a: Usually yes: dinner and breakfast are included in the per-person rate. Tell your hosts in advance about any dietary needs. Lunch is available at small cafes in the village. Alcohol is not served, and drinking in public is not appropriate.

name: Spangmik and Man homestays, Pangong
summary: The villages of Spangmik, Man and Merak on Pangong's southern shore have family homestays where you sleep in Changpa and Ladakhi homes for a fraction of camp prices, with dinner, breakfast and quiet nights by the lake.
body: Most visitors to Pangong sleep in the tented camps near Lukung and Spangmik. The saver alternative is a family homestay in Spangmik, Man or Merak, further along the shore. Rooms are simple, with thick quilts, and the family stove keeps the kitchen warm in the evening. Meals are home-cooked: rice, dal, vegetables, thukpa and butter tea.

At about 4,250 m, nights are cold even in August and hot water is limited; bathrooms are often shared, and some homes use traditional dry toilets. Power is often solar, so carry a power bank. The further you go from Spangmik towards Merak, the quieter and simpler it gets. Book through your Leh guesthouse in peak months, or ask in the villages.
why: Half the price of lakeside camps
Warm kitchens and home-cooked dinners
Quiet shore far from the day-trip crowd
price_band: ₹1,500–2,500 per person a night with dinner and breakfast (indicative)

faqs.q: Are Pangong homestays warm enough at night?
faqs.a: Families provide thick quilts and the kitchen stove is warm in the evening, but rooms are rarely heated. Nights fall below freezing even in summer. Bring a down jacket, warm hat, thermal layers and, ideally, a sleeping bag liner.

faqs.q: Which village is best for a Pangong homestay?
faqs.a: Spangmik is closest and has the most choice. Man and Merak, further along the shore, are quieter and more traditional, with fewer camps. All are reached by the same road from Tangtse; Merak adds about an hour of driving.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Pangong homestays?
faqs.a: Indians need the online Ladakh environment fee receipt and photo ID; foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit. Your homestay may record your details. Rules change, so check current status before you travel.

name: Stok Palace Heritage Hotel
summary: Rooms inside part of Stok Palace, the home of Ladakh's former royal family since the 19th century, and in the orchard below it. Stok village, across the Indus, is about 15 km from Leh and much quieter than town.
body: When Dogra forces took control of Ladakh in the 1840s, the Namgyal royal family left Leh Palace and moved to Stok, on the south side of the Indus. The palace is still the family's home, part of it is a museum of royal dress, jewellery and thangkas, and part of it has been opened as a heritage hotel with suites in the old building and newer rooms in the garden.

Staying here means traditional decor, small windows, thick walls and steps; the garden rooms are easier if stairs at altitude worry you. Stok is at a similar height to Leh, so it works for acclimatisation days, with a village to walk in and the Stok range above. A car is useful, since Leh is around 30 minutes away. Season and room types change, so check current status before you travel.
why: Sleep in the former royal family's palace
Quiet village base close to Leh
Royal museum on site

faqs.q: How far is Stok Palace from Leh?
faqs.a: Stok is about 15 km from Leh, across the Indus, roughly 30 minutes by car. Taxis between Stok and Leh cost about ₹700–1,000 one way. Having a car with driver makes day trips to the Indus valley monasteries easy.

faqs.q: Is Stok Palace Heritage Hotel open all year?
faqs.a: The hotel mainly operates in the tourist season from spring to autumn. Opening months can change from year to year, so check current status before you travel, especially for April, October and winter dates.

faqs.q: Can hotel guests visit the Stok Palace museum?
faqs.a: Yes. The museum within the palace displays royal costume, jewellery, thangkas and ceremonial objects and is open to visitors in season, usually for a fee. Ask at reception about opening hours.

name: Hotel Omasila, Leh
summary: A long-running family hotel in Changspa, the quiet green lane below Shanti Stupa, with garden seating and a short walk to cafes. It suits travellers who want comfortable, simple rooms and calm acclimatisation days without the price of Leh's larger hotels.
body: Changspa is the part of Leh many travellers end up loving: willow-lined lanes, irrigation channels, barley plots between guesthouses, and Shanti Stupa at the top of the road. Hotel Omasila is one of the older family-run hotels here, with rooms around a garden and a restaurant, and it is a comfortable place to spend the first two days doing very little.

Rooms are mid-range Ladakhi style rather than luxury: attached bathrooms, hot water, warm bedding and a sunny garden. Main Bazaar is about 15–20 minutes on foot, gently downhill, or a short taxi ride back. Ask for a lower-floor room on arrival, and check opening months if you are travelling outside the main season.
why: Quiet garden in Changspa
Walk to Shanti Stupa and cafes
Comfortable rooms at mid-range prices

faqs.q: Where is Hotel Omasila in Leh?
faqs.a: It is in Changspa, the residential and guesthouse area north-west of Main Bazaar, on the way to Shanti Stupa. The bazaar is about 15–20 minutes on foot. Taxis from the airport cost roughly ₹500–700.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Omasila open in winter?
faqs.a: Like many Leh hotels, it mainly operates from spring to autumn. Winter opening is not guaranteed, so check current status before you travel if you plan to visit between November and March.

faqs.q: Is Changspa a good area for acclimatisation?
faqs.a: Yes. It is quiet, green and flat enough for gentle walks, with cafes nearby. The climb to Shanti Stupa is best left for your third day. Book a lower-floor room for your first night so you avoid stairs.

name: The Grand Dragon Ladakh
summary: Leh's largest full-service hotel, open all year, with heated rooms, a restaurant serving Ladakhi and international food, and views to the Stok range. It is the most comfortable base in town for acclimatisation and for winter or shoulder-season trips.
body: The Grand Dragon stands on the old road south of the town centre, a short drive from Main Bazaar. It is a large, modern hotel by Ladakh standards, built with a Ladakhi look and designed to stay open through winter, which is rare in Leh. Rooms are heated and the hotel has its own restaurants and lounges, so on rest days you need not leave the building.

For signature trips we use it at the start and end of journeys, when guests are most tired and most affected by the altitude. Ask for a room facing the Stok range. It also suits winter trips for Losar or snow leopard tracking in Hemis, when most of Leh's guesthouses are closed. Check room types and current rates when you book.
why: Heated rooms, open all year
Full-service hotel for rest days
Views to the Stok range

faqs.q: Is The Grand Dragon Ladakh open in winter?
faqs.a: Yes. It is one of the few Leh hotels that stays open all year, with heated rooms, which makes it a popular base for winter trips, Losar and snow leopard tours. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How far is The Grand Dragon from Leh airport?
faqs.a: It is a short drive from the airport, around 10–15 minutes depending on traffic. Main Bazaar is about 5–10 minutes by car. The hotel can arrange airport transfers.

faqs.q: Does The Grand Dragon help with oxygen or acclimatisation?
faqs.a: Many Leh hotels keep oxygen cylinders for emergencies, and staff are used to guests feeling the altitude. Ask the hotel what is available. Oxygen is not a substitute for rest: spend at least 48 hours resting, and see a doctor if symptoms worsen.

name: Chamba Camp Thiksey
summary: The Ultimate Travelling Camp's summer camp near Thiksey Monastery, about 19 km up the Indus from Leh. Large furnished tents with private bathrooms, a dining tent and attentive service, facing one of Ladakh's most photographed gompas.
body: The Ultimate Travelling Camp runs seasonal luxury camps in India, and Chamba Camp Thiksey is its Ladakh camp, set up for the summer months near the village of Thiksey. Each tent is large and furnished like a hotel room, with a proper bed, private bathroom and heating for cold nights, and the camp has a dining tent and lounge.

The location is the point: you can be at Thiksey's morning prayers within minutes, and Hemis, Shey and Stakna are all close. It sits at roughly the same height as Leh, so the usual two lazy days on arrival apply here too. The camp generally runs from late spring to early autumn; dates and packages change, so check current status before you travel.
why: Minutes from Thiksey's morning prayers
Hotel-standard tents with private bathrooms
Close to Hemis for festival days
price_band: ₹40,000–75,000 a night for a double, usually with meals (indicative)

faqs.q: When is Chamba Camp Thiksey open?
faqs.a: It is a seasonal camp that usually runs from late spring to early autumn, roughly May to September. Exact dates change each year, so check current status before you travel and book early for Hemis festival dates.

faqs.q: Are the tents at Chamba Camp heated?
faqs.a: The tents are designed for Ladakh's cold nights, with heating and warm bedding, and each has a private bathroom. Nights still fall to near freezing in early and late season, so bring warm layers for evenings outside.

faqs.q: Is Chamba Camp a good base for acclimatisation?
faqs.a: Yes. It is quiet, at about Leh's height, with meals on site, so you can rest without going into town. Thiksey is a short drive for gentle morning outings. Still plan two lazy days before going higher.

name: Nimmu House
summary: A restored early 20th-century manor in Nimmoo village, about 35 km west of Leh near the Indus–Zanskar confluence, with heritage rooms in the house and furnished tents in its orchard garden. The best-placed fine stay for Alchi, Likir and Basgo.
body: Nimmoo is a village on the Srinagar highway where the Indus and Zanskar rivers meet. Nimmu House is an old family manor in the village that has been restored as a small hotel, with a handful of rooms in the main house and tents set among the apricot and willow trees of its garden. Meals are served in the house and garden, with Ladakhi dishes alongside European cooking.

At around 3,100 m, Nimmoo is lower than Leh, so it is a good place to sleep in the first days of a trip, and it puts Alchi, Likir, Basgo and the confluence within a short drive. It is seasonal, generally open from spring to autumn. Check current status, dates and room types before you travel.
why: Restored village manor with garden tents
Lower than Leh, good for early nights
Short drive to Alchi, Likir and Basgo
price_band: ₹18,000–35,000 a night for a double, usually with meals (indicative)

faqs.q: How far is Nimmu House from Leh?
faqs.a: Nimmoo is about 35 km west of Leh on the Srinagar highway, roughly 45 minutes to an hour by car. Alchi is about 30 km further west. The airport transfer is easy to arrange.

faqs.q: Is Nimmu House open all year?
faqs.a: No. It is a seasonal property, generally open from spring to autumn. Dates change each year, so check current status before you travel if you are planning April or October.

faqs.q: Is Nimmu House good for the first nights in Ladakh?
faqs.a: Yes. At around 3,100 m, it is lower than Leh, and the garden is a calm place to rest. We often place guests here after one or two nights in Leh, or as the second stop of a gentle itinerary.

name: Lchang Nang Retreat, Nubra
summary: A cottage retreat in the poplar and willow groves of Tegar village, near Sumur on the Nubra arm of the valley. Open from about May to mid-October, it is the most polished place to stay in Nubra and a calm base for Diskit, Hunder and Panamik.
body: Lchang Nang sits in Tegar village on the quieter Nubra river side of the valley, away from the camps at Hunder. Cottages are spread through a garden of poplar and willow, with views to the mountains, and meals use vegetables and fruit from the valley wherever possible.

At about 3,100 m, Nubra is lower than Leh, so a night or two here helps after the Khardung La crossing. From Tegar, Samstanling gompa at Sumur is a short drive, and Diskit, Hunder and the Panamik hot springs are within easy reach. Turtuk is a long day trip. The retreat is seasonal; check current status and dates before you travel.
why: Quietest arm of Nubra
Cottages in a garden of trees
Good base after Khardung La
price_band: ₹20,000–40,000 a night for a double, usually with meals (indicative)

faqs.q: Where is Lchang Nang Retreat?
faqs.a: It is in Tegar village near Sumur, on the Nubra river side of the valley, about 125 km from Leh via Khardung La. Diskit and Hunder are about an hour away. Drive from Leh takes 4.5–5.5 hours including stops.

faqs.q: When is Lchang Nang Retreat open?
faqs.a: It generally opens from about May to mid-October, depending on the season and road conditions over Khardung La. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Lchang Nang suitable for children and older travellers?
faqs.a: Yes. The cottages are on level garden paths, the valley is lower than Leh, and meals are on site. The main challenge is the drive over Khardung La at 5,359 m; spend two or three nights in Leh first and keep the stop at the pass short.
